notes: This paper presents a THEORETICAL PREDICTION of the axion mass and decay constant, NOT an experimental exclusion limit or measured constraint. The authors perform numerical simulations of axion production from cosmic strings in the early universe and combine results with lattice QCD topological susceptibility data (Borsanyi et al. 2016) to predict that if the axion comprises 100% of dark matter, then m_a = 26.2 ± 3.4 µeV and f_a = (2.21 ± 0.29) × 10^11 GeV. The main result is a single point on the f_a-m_a plane derived from cosmological assumptions (PQ symmetry restoration post-inflation, standard FRW cosmology, axion as 100% DM). This is NOT a measured exclusion limit from an experiment, but rather a cosmological prediction. The coupling_type AxionMass is appropriate because the paper's primary result is the f_a-m_a relationship itself. The data point represents the predicted values with their 1-sigma uncertainties.
